inputs.share_count_basis: FY2026 10-K diluted weighted-average shares (combined Class A + Class B, the basis BF-B's own reported EPS uses); held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in owner FCF -- charging both would double-count. FY2026 buybacks ($400M) are the funding mechanism for the flat count, not a value driver.
inputs.sbc_source: BF-B_Metrics.csv StockBasedComp column (cash-flow-statement add-back), sourced from SEC XBRL. Equity-award withholding taxes not material/not separately disclosed at scale here (KPI history shows $1-4M/yr in years it appears) and are not added on top.
inputs.wacc_rationale: 8% built from a US risk-free rate (~4.2% 10yr UST) plus an equity risk premium and a small size/leverage premium appropriate to a $12B-mkt-cap branded consumer-staples company with ~1.8x net debt/EBITDA and ~10x interest coverage -- moderate, not distressed, leverage. No separate scenario-specific WACC adjustment: risk is carried in the growth/margin paths and the probability weights, not stacked again in the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: not material -- Brown-Forman's operating leases (offices, some warehousing) are immaterial relative to owned distilleries/warehouses; no separate lease adjustment made.
inputs.nci_treatment: none -- wholly owned operations, no reported minority interest.
inputs.notes: FRESH BUILD, no prior DCF/Drivers file existed. Routed via .claude/skills/dcf-methods/SKILL.md to the owner-FCF component DCF (standard branded consumer-products operating company); no non-US/cyclical adaptations needed (USD filer, USD quote, no leases/NCI of consequence). MODEL BASIS NOTE: Brown-Forman's reported 'EBITDA' in the Metrics CSV is GAAP EBITDA (OperatingIncome + D&A) with SBC already expensed inside operating income -- NOT an adjusted-EBITDA-ex-SBC figure the way a tech comparable reports it. To stay compatible with the engine's component formula (which subtracts sbc_pct from ebitda_margin_path to reach owner EBITDA), ebitda_margin_path below is built SBC-ADDED-BACK (GAAP EBITDA + SBC, as % of revenue): FY2026 actual on that basis is 28.6% (1093+32)/3928, FY2025 30.7%, FY2024 (peak) 36.5%. FCF-BASE NORMALIZATION: FY2026 reported FCF of $893M / owner FCF of $861M is NOT used as last_fcf -- OCF jumped from $598M (FY2025) to $1,000M (FY2026) on a working-capital swing (almost certainly a barreled-whiskey/agave aging-inventory drawdown tied to the Jan-2025 restructuring and softer volumes) while net income fell FY2025->FY2026 ($869M->$715M). Reconstructing the same reported-fcf-minus-sbc calculation for FY2023/24/25 gives owner FCF of $439M/$394M/$403M (9.4-10.4% margins) -- a consistent, much lower base. last_fcf=356.0 is instead the model's OWN first projected year (FY2027) built bottom-up from components at guided margins, deliberately calibrated to land close to but modestly below that FY23-25 historical range, consistent with FY2027 guidance of a further organic operating-income decline. CAPEX_PCT CONVENTION: capex_pct_path below is a COMBINED capex + structural working-capital reinvestment rate, not capex alone. Reported capex (2.7-5.5% of revenue historically) badly understates BF-B's true cash reinvestment: whiskey and tequila require multi-year barrel/barrica aging, so the business continuously invests real cash in growing aged-inventory stock as a normal-course (not growth-linked) outflow -- reverse-engineering FY2023/2024/2025 (NOPAT+D&A-capex vs actual owner FCF) implies a working-capital-and-other cash drag of -7.3%/-15.2%/-8.1% of revenue in those years respectively (average ~-10%, excluding no year), on top of reported capex of 4.3%/5.5%/4.2%. The engine's wc_capture_pct mechanic (applied to the CHANGE in revenue) cannot represent a drag that persists even when revenue is flat or falling, as this one does -- so the bulk of the structural inventory-investment drag is folded into capex_pct_path (~10-12%, moderating slightly over the horizon as restructuring reduces inventory intensity) and wc_capture_pct is held to a small residual (-2 to -4%) capturing genuine growth-linked AR/payables dynamics only. This is a deliberate, disclosed deviation from a literal reading of the component formula, made because the alternative (applying the formula literally) would have overstated Year-1 FCF by ~80% against BF-B's own three-year actual conversion rate. Historical growth CAGRs are computed on this same reported_fcf-minus-sbc owner-FCF series.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: blended judgment, not a single CAGR
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (8.6% 5yr / 7.1% 3yr) diverges sharply from revenue (2.6%/-2.4%) and EPS (-4.1%/-2.1%), and the reported FCF 3yr CAGR (25.2%) is an artifact of the FY2026 working-capital drawdown, not underlying growth (owner-FCF 3yr CAGR on a like-for-like basis would be roughly flat-to-down, not +25%/yr -- see inputs.notes). Equity is compounding on retained earnings and buybacks reducing the share count even as revenue and EPS have fallen for two straight years; it is not a reliable growth proxy here and was NOT used as the base-case growth anchor. Base-case revenue growth (selected_growth_rate 2.5% terminal, flat in FY2027 per guidance) is instead built directly from management's own FY2027 guidance and the qualitative growth/risk balance in the Analysis JSON, not from a mechanical CAGR pick.

base.narrative: FY2027 organic net sales flat and organic operating income down 3-5% exactly as guided (Sept-2026 Q1 release, reaffirmed from June-2026 FY2026 year-end guidance); adjusted-EBITDA margin bottoms around 27.5-28% in FY2027-28 as tariff costs, the US distributor-network transition, and continued Jack Daniel's US softness offset early restructuring savings, then recovers gradually toward ~30-31% by year 8-10 as the $70-80M annualized restructuring savings fully land, the distributor transition completes, and emerging-markets/travel-retail growth (currently double-digit) becomes a larger share of the mix -- but margin never returns to FY2024's cyclical peak of 36.5% (SBC-added-back basis), reflecting a structurally softer US spirits/RTD category and a Gen-Z moderation trend that is a genuine secular headwind, not a one-year blip. Revenue growth resumes modestly (1-2.5%) as the distributor transition normalizes and emerging markets offset developed-market weakness, settling at a mature 2.5% terminal rate.

bull.narrative: US distributor-network realignment and the $70-80M restructuring savings land faster and more completely than guided, tariffs are resolved without material EBIT drag (following the EU's decision not to retaliate against American whiskey), and premiumization (Woodford Reserve, Old Forester, Herradura super-premium) plus RTD/RTP innovation (Tennessee Blackberry, New Mix) and double-digit emerging-market/travel-retail growth more than offset continued US softness. Adjusted-EBITDA margin recovers to 34.5% by maturity -- still below the FY2024 peak of 36.5%, since even the bull case does not assume the pre-restructuring cost structure returns, but well above the current trough. Scarcity value (the 2026 Pernod Ricard and Sazerac approaches) is not modelled as a takeout premium here, consistent with the dual-class structure giving the Brown family sole discretion over any transaction.

bear.narrative: Jack Daniel's US volume decline proves structural rather than cyclical as Gen-Z moderation deepens and the RTD category keeps decelerating; the EU or another major export market imposes a material retaliatory tariff on American whiskey (Bernstein's cited scenario of a 50% EU tariff cutting BF-B EBIT by roughly 10% materializes in some form), the Canadian retail boycott persists or widens, and the US distributor-network transition causes shelf-placement and inventory-timing disruption through FY2028 rather than resolving by FY2027 as guided. Restructuring savings partly offset but do not reverse the decline, and the CEO transition adds execution risk during a period the company can least afford it. Revenue contracts through FY2028 before stabilizing at a much-reduced base; margin never recovers past 26%. The business remains solidly FCF-positive throughout (interest coverage ~10x, net debt/EBITDA ~1.8x per Analysis JSON) -- this is a margin-compression bear case, not a going-concern one, so the bear weight is not pushed as high as it would be for a leveraged or single-customer name.

scenario_narratives.base: FY2027 guidance (flat organic sales, -3% to -5% organic operating income) plays out roughly as stated; margin bottoms in FY2027-28 and recovers gradually as restructuring savings and the distributor transition land, but the mature margin settles below the FY2024 cyclical peak because US category softness and Gen-Z moderation are treated as a partial structural change, not a one-year dip.
scenario_narratives.bull: Restructuring and distributor realignment execute cleanly, tariffs resolve favorably, and emerging-market/RTD growth outpaces US decline enough to drive margin back close to (but still below) the FY2024 peak.
scenario_narratives.bear: US whiskey/RTD softness proves structural, a major export tariff bites, the Canadian boycott persists, and the distributor transition disrupts execution into FY2028 -- a multi-year margin-compression scenario, not a solvency one.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear weight raised from the 15% house default to 25% because three concrete, currently-live headwinds (unquantified tariff exposure that management itself says it cannot size, an active CEO transition, and a US distributor-network overhaul) are stacked simultaneously on top of two straight years of EPS decline (-29% FY2024-FY2026) -- more concurrent unresolved risk than a typical mature consumer-staples name carries. Bull weight trimmed to 25% (from 35%) to match, since the bull case requires several of those same things (tariffs, distributor transition, CEO succession) to resolve well at once rather than just one. This is a margin-compression/execution risk profile, not a going-concern one (interest coverage ~10x), so bear is not pushed to the 30%+ reserved for solvency-risk names.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Brown-Forman is a mature, moderately-levered branded spirits company (Jack Daniel's, Woodford Reserve, Herradura) trading at a genuine cyclical/structural trough: two straight years of EPS decline (-29% FY2024-FY2026), guided to a third (FY2027 organic operating income -3% to -5%), against unresolved tariff risk, an active CEO search, and a US distributor-network overhaul. The valuation deliberately does NOT extrapolate the FY2026 reported FCF spike (a working-capital/inventory-drawdown artifact) or the FY2024 margin peak; it builds forward from guided near-term trough margins and a moderate, partial recovery as restructuring savings and the distributor transition land, capped well below the historical peak to reflect a structurally softer US spirits category. The 2026 Pernod Ricard and Sazerac approaches are read as evidence of scarcity value, not modelled as a takeout scenario, since the Brown family's voting control makes any transaction entirely discretionary to them.
key_risks_to_valuation: Tariff exposure is explicitly unquantifiable by management; a severe scenario (e.g., a reinstated/expanded EU tariff) could cut EBIT materially beyond what the bear case assumes
Jack Daniel's brand concentration -- a large majority of profit rests on one flagship franchise now seeing US volume declines
Dual-class structure means public BF-B holders cannot force any value-realizing transaction regardless of how undervalued the stock becomes
CEO transition risk during a simultaneous distributor-network overhaul

The capex_pct_path used here embeds a judgment call (structural aging-inventory investment folded into capex rather than modelled as a separate line) that a reader should sanity-check against future 10-Ks as explicit inventory-investment disclosure becomes available
